body: Excellent visit here. We were taken round by a friendly and engaging guide, and learnt lotsabout tea production in a short space of time.Atmospheric place which offers a chance to taste various teas and a pleasant gift/souvenir buying experience (no pressure). Glad we stopped here.

body: Great guided tour of the museum taking you through the tea manufacturing process. Would recommend to get more information on the Sri Lankan tea history.

body: Visited Ceylon Tea Museum with our 16 year old who enjoys a hot brew! We were very impressed by the young girl who took us for a tour, she was very informative and spoke very good English. We enjoyed our free cuppa at the end and also shared a 1000LKR sample of many other types. We actually ended up drinking so much tea that we gave ourselves a stomach ache 😂 This was totally self inflicted!!Well worth a visit
title: Very informative

body: We had a lovely visit to the Ceylon Tea Museum in Kandy! The setting itself is quite charming, housed in a restored tea factory with lots of character. We really enjoyed the brief but informative tour, where one of the team members walked us through the historical tea-making process — it was a nice mix of education and storytelling without feeling too long or formal.Included in the entry price was a relaxing cup of freshly brewed tea, which we enjoyed in a calm setting with great views from the top of the factory. There’s also a small gift shop on-site; we didn’t feel pushed into purchasing at all — lots of different teas for those interested.Overall, it offered a great insight into the history of tea in Sri Lanka. We took a Tuk Tuk both ways via Uber, which was convenient and added a bit of local flavor to the outing. Would definitely recommend it for a peaceful, culturally rich hour or two in Kandy.
title: Charming Slice of Tea History in Kandy

body: Please go there to learn so much of Sri Lanka's Tea verities . Most People are going there to study the sri lankan Tea. it,s in Kandy
title: Experience about Ceylon Tea Museum

body: This is a fascinating place with much to learn; however, the staff seemed rather rushed in their explanations of the tea-making process. After a complimentary cup of tea, they were quite eager to sell and push their products. We purchased four small tins of tea for @$200 Australian dollars, only to find the same tea later in Colombo at a significantly lower price. The tour proved to be quite expensive. I would advise caution.
title: Buyer beware. To Tea or not to tea

body: super interesting visit especially when it rains. we had a good time without too many tourists I recommend!A little far off though so good to have a guide
title: interesting

body: Hidden as it is, up in the hills over Kandy, the Ceylon Tea Museum is a definite find to remember when one finally discovers the place. Not much known among the travelers and being far from the maddening crowds, this museum is well worth a couple of hours. Definitely not for one who wants to rush in and out, this place needs time for the feel and taste of it to blend in- just like the product for which the place is dedicated to itself. Comprehensive and excellently displayed, in terms of organisation and clarity, the patient visitor is guaranteed to discover a good deal of the history of Ceylon where Tea played its part- in the century old machines, artifacts, well described notices and of course the sense of the place which in fact had been a tea factory a century or more in age. A t the top floor the Tea canteen awaits with a free cup of Black Tea with options to try out a whole array of different blends.Road is fine and the morning is a better time.Cost, affordable.
title: A place what's well worth to blend in for two hours.

body: Nice tour and tea tasting. The Bird Park is also worth a visit. Nice for walking. Nice drive there.
title: Nice

body: After reading reviews about tea factory tours and not finding anything acceptable, we chose to go to the tea museum. A good choice too. We were shown round the museum by a very informed guide who knew all the answers to our sometimes obscure questions. There was a lovely exhibition of old and new photographs depicting the life of a tea picker. A welcome free cup of tea and a not overpriced gift shop.Highly recommendedLKR 1000 per person entry for foreignersClosed on Mondays

body: This is a museum, not a working tea factory. However for a small entry fee they take you on an informative tour of all the various museum pieces and explain how it all worked in those times. The museum is in an old multi story tea factory. We id this museum and also a working tea factory which was a good combination. Staff were great and spoke excellent English.

body: A more than 100 years old tea factory keeping the original machinery purchased around 1880 kept on display showcasing the technology then. body: A great experience. Loved the tea experience. Really exciting to learn about this commercial product and I have become a tea lover now

body: If you want to learn a bit about the history of tea in Sri Lanka this is a great place to visit. Lots of wonderful old machinery and all sorts of interesting displays. Fascinating and well worth a visit!

body: After a lot of Temples and relics it was interesting to see the history of tea and the way it is dried and sorted and graded - worth visiting and fun to have tea in their shop and of course buy tea!

body: Being a long resident and visitor to Kandy for over thirty years I have taken many guests to this museum over the years but not for a few years until recently. I was shocked to see the decline of this museum and the poor visitor experience it now offers. The museum itself is tired and dilapidated with no sign of any real care being taken to maintain it. A lot of areas are just empty spaces, dingy and dusty in the main.Worst of all is standard of welcome, with staff simply going through the motions, indifferent to visitors to the point of rudeness. This attraction clearly needs to be much better managed to reflect the fine heritage of tea growing in Sri Lanka.It is definitely not worth the time and expense involved in a visit. My advice is to find a working tea factory that is open to visitors. You will see and learn much more and certainly receive a better welcome than at the Tea Museum.A real disgrace to Sri Lankan tourism to have let this place go to such ruin.

body: The Ceylon tea museum is located in the hills of Hantane, about a 20min drive from the Kandy town.It's open from 0830hrs-1545hrs Tuesdays-SaturdaysIt's open from 0830hrs-1500hrs on SundaysIt's closed on Mondays & all full moon (poya) daysIt costs Rs50 for locals & Rs800 for foreigners.Quite fittingly, the museum building itself is an old & once used tea factory. It has a lot of old tea factory machines which were used in different factories back in the day & were later donated to the museum.You can have a 15-20min tour in English or in Sinhalese where the tour guide will explain the whole process of making tea; from picking the tea leaves to the tasty elixir in your cup.S/he will also explain the history of tea in Sri Lanka & how it all began, what the different machines do, show you a mini model of a functioning tea factory, show you an 80 year old tea plant, the oldest available tea packet of SL, & more. However, you need time on your own to go through some of the information.The building itself has 4 storeys so there's a lot to see, including some old equipment used many years ago. At the top is a small cafe where you're served a complimentary cup of tea & there is also a tea shop.If by chance the tour guides are all busy, I recommend waiting until 1 is available, because the information is interesting & important. If you're a tea fan, this is a must see, but even if you're not, this is some nice time spent.
title: A fitting museum for the country which produces the best black tea

body: A lovely place to visit if you are really into tea and the history behind one of our absolute most popular drinks all over the world!

body: The museum is about 10km away from downtown Kandy, so we took a tuk-tuk, which was not expensive. Without being asked, the driver waited for us, while we were inside, so we volunteered a small waiting fee. I cannot over-emphasise how wonderful the museum is. My companion and I had a guide just for us (we were the only guests present for most of the time) and she was totally brilliant. My pal has an engineering background, and I'm a chemist, so we had some pretty deep questions for her, which she answered terrifically. I learned a heck of a lot about tea, which is good, cos being a Brit, I've drunk it all my life!Speaking of Britishness, we were fascinated by how much of the antique processing equipment had been brought in from the UK, including some hydro-electric turbines made in the English Lake District! I enjoyed the quality control laboratory, as I once worked in QC.The cup of tea at the end of the visit was very welcome, and most enjoyable.This museum was one of the highlights of our entire trip.I bought a small amount of tea (not expensive), and I'm sipping it as I write this. Delicious!
title: Superb in every way!

title: Informative and nice designed place

body: A pleasant way to spend a morning. Your ticket for entry includes a guided tour of the museum along with a cup of delicious Ceylon tea at the end of the tour. Interesting history of this factory which is no longer in operation. Negotiate no more than 1000LKR for a round-trip tuk-tuk to the tea factory.
title: Interesting history - and a pleasant cup of tea!

body: My most favourite of all tea factories and attractions I've seen in Sri Lanka. Very well done both the museum and the tour. I highly recommend in combination with a running tea factory.
title: Jewel among the tea attractions

body: I went to four tea factories in Sri Lanka in a short period of time, and this was the most informative one. We were lucky to have a knowledgeable guide who spoke clear English. The fact that this is a quiet "museum factory" also made it a lot easier to actually take in the information.The oral guiding is complemented by a good video shown in the tea room, where you can enjoy a good cup after the tour. There are also additional displays there for those who remain intellectually curious.There is a small tea store, but no hard sell at all.
title: Very informative

body: There are many old machines. Books,documents books and pictures are displayed.there.Nice visit it is worth to visit.It explains about Srilanka Ceylon tea history,
title: Historical place.

body: I was suprised by how interesting this museum was. After a trip to a tea factory the day before, I thought I was all tea'd out. But I found this museum much more interesting. The guide was very informative, and the museum is very well done. The preservation of the old machines is World class. The timber lining of the building is pure 1930's style and design. There is not the usual pressure to buy anything, and you get a pot of brew at the end. It you only want one tea visit, make it this one.
title: The only tea visit you need to do.

body: The museum and displays are good and the guide taking us around was good, but the descriptions and process seemed to be a scripted without much time to ask questions. Felt like it was a way of getting us around a s quickly as possible so hopefully we would buy something at the shop.
title: Good but heavily scrpited

body: I visited this place along with my friends when we were on holiday.It had the whole history as to how the plantations started in the country and was well elaborated.A best choice for a tour around the country.
title: One of the best places for a trip!

body: I did learn a thing or two at the tea museum, however, I found it overpriced for such a short tour that ended with a mediocre cup of tea.
title: Did learn a thing or two

body: This is probably as good as a free visit to a tea factory could be. It's interesting to see how they make all the different kinds of tea and how it's all sorted out. After the free tour they take you upstairs to the cafe and your given a free cup of tea to try. Your expected to buy something afterwards but we didn't and this wasn't an issue
title: Worth a look

body: As previous reviewers have mentioned this is a great place to come if:- you want to learn more about the tea industry and history of tea in Sri Lanka- you want something to do to stay cool during the heat of Kandy I enjoyed it as I have quite an interest in colonial history and the tea industry. My wife was not so keen and preferred our experience at a working factory. The price of entry has risen and I feel is pushing it slightly for what is on offer. You will also need to outlay for a three wheeler to get here and back.Having been to a working tea factory the machinery and process section wasn’t overly impressive. However our guide was wonderful, very knowledgeable and with great English. Also the working model of a factory was great though! In contrast the collection of historical artefacts was really interesting and nicely displayed.The cup of tea at the end was delicious and as ever service was excellent. If you are interested in tea it’s well worth a visit.
title: Interesting, superb guide but a little overpriced

body: Located at Hantane, the 1925 vintage Ceylon Tea Museum is one of the important attractions of the hill country, Kandy in Sri Lanka. The Tea Museum is a building of four floors where from ground floor to second floor it’s all old machineries, library and auditorium. For purchasing lip smacking variety and flavors of Sri Lankan tea one must visit the third floor which is sales unit. The fourth floor comprises of a magnificent restaurant where one can enjoy a free cup and the captivating and breathtaking surrounding view of the hill country from the top. One can visualize Matale Range and Kunckles Range through a telescope positioned here. From the top it’s an encircling view of green landscape comprising tea plantations of myriad types. Location: Hantane Road, Kandy
title: Vintage Ceylon Tea Museum

body: The museum is open for public from Tuesday to Sunday and is closed on Mondays. Opening hours are 8.30 a.m. to 4.00 p.m. You must enter the museum before 3.30 p.m. On Sundays and public holidays it will be closed at 3 p.m. I advise to go there at least one and half hour before the closure and then you can relax and enjoy the tour. If there is ` public holiday (ex:Poya day) on weekends ,the Museum is opened til 3 p.m. if it's week day, it will be closed. Kandy, Ceylon Tea Museum is a must see event for locals as well as tourists also to get an understanding about the inception of the tea industry. The location of Kandy, Ceylon Tea Museum is very beautiful and it is at Hantane which is 2 k.m. from Kandy and need 10 minute to reach there if there is not traffic. The entry fee is Rs 750 for a tourist, per person. There are about 4 levels to this building and at the 3rd level has several tea boutiques to purchase tea from if you wish to do so. I suggest any tourist to buy tea from this place as it is cheaper compared to prices of tea in tourist stores in Colombo. The manager speaks good English. The staff is always ready to explain about the history of tea industry of Sri Lanka. The visit is more interesting for tea drinkers all over the world. It was a fabulous afternoon seeing a tea bud and two leaves from the tree being picked and plucked and how it is processed to the end product. Kandy, Ceylon Tea Museum is well organised an it is a lovely building, with superb breathtaking views from its windows. When we were there a guide accompanied us around the exhibitions telling us about the history of the tea industry in Sri Lanka and provided information on the manufacturing process. We enjoyed reading about the history of the tea plantations of Sri Lanka. Everything you need to know for the tea in Sri Lanka. You can discover the production of tea with all the machines, archives, old photos and few different shops where you can buy locally produced tea.. If you are really interested in the tea business or an aficionado of beautifully restored vintage British agricultural machinery, this museum is well worth the effort. We found it to be a worthwhile complement to a visit to a working tea estate up in the mountains. It is very much a static museum, with no processing going on. Included in the admission price is a cup of tea offered at the end of the visit.it located about 2 km from Kandy city ,it need 10 minute to reach [if there are not traffic ] it is interesting all as when you visit you can have some different feelings and knowledge about history of Ceylon Tea The shops were very nice with good prices and friendly staff. However no cards accepted here. It is must visit place when you are in Kandy of Sri Lanka (as “Ceylon Tea” in the past) which is better known in the world for its finest tea and this the most appropriate place to learn about its rich history and to take first hand experience in the processes done in which hard labored tea leaves becoming a nice stimulating beverage in front of your own eye. I recommend you to visit Kandy, Ceylon Tea Museum.
title: At Kandy, Ceylon Tea Museum See & Get Explanations about the History of Tea Industry of Sri Lank.

body: This is a nice Tea Museum about Ceylon tea. Further they have good collection of tea processing machines antiques. However not having multimedia guide or guided tour is a huge vacuum. Multimedia guide or guided tour could have add lot of value to this well kept Museum. Even the presentation is suburb, there is not sufficient information on how tea processing happen, sequence of the processes etc. etc. Still for tea lovers this is a must visit place. This is not a crowded place. When I went there around 10:00 am on a Sunday, I was the only visitor. However, when I came out more tourists were comings in. Little more publicity could have bring lot of people to this place.
title: Nice Tea Museum, multimedia / guided tour could have made this great

body: is located in an old tea factory in Kany, on the outskirts of Kandy. The entrance fee includes a guided tour of the building, introducing both the machinery of the 19th century and the process of making tea. The optional tour is quite informative.The building is full of original machinery such as the Little Giant Tea Roller, which twists dried tea leaves into spirals for cutting. There are also archival prints of 19th century industry, including the life and work of tea pioneer James Taylor. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a cup of tea while taking in a panoramic view from the fourth floor of the ex-factory.The factory is a pleasant three-wheeler ride up from Kandy and is well worth a visit!
title: The Ceylon Tea Museum

body: The museum very quiet when visited (there were more staff present than visitors). We found the tour interesting and enjoyed learning about the history of tea. You get s free cup of tea included and there are several stores selling tea which makes ideal souveniers
title: Worth a visit

body: We went to the Tea Museum based on reviews on TA and th expectations were not very high. To our pleasant surprise, it turned out to be a good visit. The guide was very knowledgeable and patient. She explained various steps involved in tea making. The tea tasting experience was also good. My daughter enjoyed the ice tea available at a nominal price, while I sipped BOP tea.
title: Highly recommend

body: Must to visit this place, where you can learn how tea was made and see the varieties of tea with a cup of tea for free.
title: Great experience

body: Based in the hills above Kandy, the Ceylon Tea Museum is a short tuk tuk journey away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre. The museum is based in a former tea factory but it retains all the equipment used in early tea production and paints a clear picture of the tea production process and how it evolved. Included in the cheap entry cost is an informative guided tour and a cup of tea. There are also a number of shops in the building selling tea at the end of the tour. The whole visit takes less than a couple of hours and is a good chance to escape the midday heat.
title: All you need to know about tea!

body: This is a good trip to take if you have a spare hour or two whilst in Kandy. The museum is about 20 -30 mins in a tuk tuk from Kandy city centre (depending on the traffic getting out of Kandy!) And the free guided tour at the museum takes around 20 minutes also.Interesting collection of old tea factory items as well as some good information on the history of tea. There is a free cup of tea at the end of the tour and also some shops where you can buy different types of tea.
title: Interesting trip with a free cup of tea

body: This is a gem of a museum, hidden away outside Kandy. It features very personalized tours including a nice cup of tea through an original old tea factory. The guided tour is included in the ticket price and is very friendly and informative. The gift shop has a wide selection of local tea to take home. A must see in Kandy!
title: Great experience

body: The Ceylon Tea Museum is a place that anyone can learn about the history of Ceylon Tea and the varieties of Tea that are present. I have been visiting this museum over five times and each time I want to visit more and more. During my last visit I was happy to see everything newly renovated.
title: Informative & Beautiful

body: Old buildings with tea experience-Some old machines are displayed,we enjoyed this visit,You can study about Ceylon tea there.Dont miss it.
title: History of Ceylon tea,can understand there.little bit away from the city.

body: A nice educating museum located in an old tea factory just few km out of Kandy. We received an English tour, which was very interesting. Entrance fee was reasonable and the staff was very friendly. Gave us a lot of information and interesting details about tea growing in general and about Sri-Lanka's tea production and plantations.definitely worth a visit (with a complimentary cup of tea at the end of the tour).
title: A great experience.

body: Located in old tea factory among the teagardens, the museum provides an informative insight into development of the tea industry that make Sri Lanka famous
title: worthy of your visit

body: A great visit. It was so interesting and the guide was extremely informative. It was great to see and understand the history of Ceylon tea. Definitely recommend!!
title: We loved it!

body: We got a great insight into the process of making tea with our guided tour around the museum. The guide was very friendly and a free cup of tea was provided at the end of the tour. All in all, a pleasant place to visit.
title: Pop in for a Cuppa!

body: Very interesting to see the process of preparing tea leaves. The museum is worth visiting to see and read about some of the history. The guided tour was appreciative to see what processes occur in the preparation of tea. The surrounds are lovely, and you can see tea leaves being picked.
title: Buzz of history in a lovely setting

body: We stopped here on our way to Kandy for an hour or so. It was quiet when we arrived, although a tour group turned up just as we were heading out.After paying the entrance fee we had a whistle stop tour of the machinery and process, before heading upstairs for the complementary tea. You are encouraged to have a look round the different vendors located the floor down from the cafe, but it is not required. We bought a few gifts from one of the shops though, as there is a reasonable selection.Worth visiting if you're in the area, and you're interested in tea and the tea making process (my partner enjoyed it!).
title: Pleasant staff with tour and shops

body: My husband was more interested than me... They show how the tea was made years ago. I am not sure I would go if he did not ask for it.
title: If you like tea...

body: I learned so much about the making of tea on this trip. It was just wonderful. It's a great cultural lesson as well when it comes to British imperialism and the tea trade. I think I was just oblivious to the history behind it.
title: Great Tour

body: Nothing special given the outrageous entry fees; one can visit other tea factories in and around the hill country much more cheaply (if not free) - and see the production process to boot. If one has no time and only in Kandy, fair enough; otherwise, give it a miss!
title: Not worth it - Unless this is your only time in the hill country

body: We took a tuk tuk up to the museum expecting an engaging experience. My expectations were not met. We were shown around the museum by a lovely hostess after paying our admission fees. We saw machinery used in the tea making process from the C19. We were then entitled to a 'free' tea, included in the admission fee. There was no description of which tea it was ie which region. I can only assume that it wasn't Kandy as apparently tea from Kandy is best consumed with milk. I'm not a tea drinker so wasn't overly concerned. There was a video in the tea room outlining the history of tea in Sri Lanka. I found the video the most engaging part; until it stopped short of the end. We ventured into an area that was part of the tea plantation and again this was underwhelming as it appears that the area in close proximity, where we were advised to go, is no longer part of a plantation. The insight into the 'human element' of the tea plantation was best observed from the tuk tuk where we observed the shacks the tea pickers lived in, from the road. Very rudimentary conditions. Maybe I didn't do enough research in advance of heading up the hill. Unless you're a tea lover fascinated by the historical presence an processes involved in the tea making process, I'd give this a skip. I'm interested in the human element and the landscape of tea plantations and I clearly went to the wrong spot.
title: Underwhelming

body: Having seen enough temples, my wife and I decided to visit the Tea Museum instead. Although they levy a charge, you are given value for money, unlike many other things and sights we experienced in Sri Lanka. A guide goes along with you to explain the use of all the displayed machines and the processing of tea leaves. It is very informative. At the end, you are also given a very nice cup of tea!
title: Well Worth Visiting

body: A lovely tea museum situated atop Hantana. The weather is different and you will feel like you are in a much colder clime than Kandy. Tea is tasty. They have small boutiques to sell them as well. You can read a lot of history here. A wonderful place to visit.
title: A Lovely Place...

body: Guides so knowledgable and friendly, definitely worth the 800Rs entry fee. There were no negatives about this visit - it was amazing to learn so much about tea. Much better value than temple of the tooth
title: Surprisingly amazing

body: I really enjoyed coming to this place. I did not expect much as it was located in such rural area. There was a guided tour, free tea, and tea market where I could get some discount to get tea!
title: Very serene environment, good tea!

body: Arriving at the Tea Museum seemed it had not much to offer but as one walks it way through the various levels one can appreciate the educational Tea history this museum has to add to ones knowledge.It wonderful to note how Tea originated and the equipment used to process tea for everyday consumption.The complimentary tea is refreshing while watching the tea documentary on the TV.
title: Educational

body: Worth a short visit if you have the time, especially if you're a tea connoisseur. The exhibitions provide some interesting information about tea production in the region. Be sure to sample some tea at the end of the tour!
title: Interesting insights into history of tea and manufacturing process

body: A bit of an overpriced tourist trap aimed at selling you teas from boutiques on the top floor. However they did educate us about the different types of Ceylon tea and James Taylor so the trip wasn't totally wasted. I would say though buy your tea from the supermarket not the tourist shops.
title: A bit of a tourist trap

body: Rather overpriced and the guide was not very engaging, though there is a old school cage elevator still in operation which was pretty interesting. If your interest is in understanding the tea making process as opposed to looking at all the machines on display in the museum, would suggest visiting an operating tea factory instead - the Halpewatte tour in Ella was very good and a lot more affordably priced at 300 lkr
title: Overpriced and not very engaging

body: Old factory turned into a museum with refurbished production equipment. Guides are so knowledgable and patient that they won't let any questions unanswered.I would likely recommend the visit to anybody, tea enthusiast or not !Stay for the tea tasting on upper floor and watch the documentary, highly instructive too.
title: Must do for tea enthusiasts !

body: Stayed with my wife in this hotel on our trip across Sri Lanka. By far the coolest one with a combination of real factory installations and English Victorian style. Clean, friendly and nicely situated.
title: Awesome - Tea factory turned into a hotel.

body: Ask your guide to take you there. For 800rupees you get a guided tour and a tasty ceylon tea. Staff was nice and smilling all the time
title: Hidden place with a lot of history

body: We struggled to find this place, arrived an hour before closing time and wish we had longer. Entrance fee 800 rupee per adult includes a cup of fresh tea which is particularly delicious. The museum guides are very engaging and eager to share their knowledge of the tea production process. We learnt lots, it is not as straight forward as one may assume. There is much hard work in gruelling temperatures to create the tea for a cuppa. It is humbling to learn of the history.
title: Hard to find the museum but worth the visit

body: Enjoyed learning about the history of tea processing, but wasn't really worth the entrance fee when we can visit government run organizations in Kandy that offer essentially the same info for free
title: Informative visit

body: An interesting place to visit for tea lovers or any other. An old factory turned into a museum has all the machines and information of everything that has been used in the making of Tea,A worthwhile visit. Hantana where it is situated is accessible, and scenic drive to get to the place. Quite close to kandy townMuch of tea country of Hantana is now residential but plantations are yet maintained.Sales outlets are there to buy teas of different flavours.Just try it!
title: My cup of Tea!!!!

body: Want to know more about tea then be sure to visit this place and follow it with a cup of tea like you have never tasted before . Sales people but NOT pushy
title: Informative tour

body: We were shown all the old machines and the process the tea leaves went through to end up in our cup. Floors 2 and 3 didnt have much and the top floor was where you got your cup of tea
title: Quite interesting

body: The shop has an extensive range of teas with the chance to sample some of the blends. The prices are average for Sri Lanka. The factory tour will give those with no knowledge enough to ponder when they sip their tea back home. The hard labour that goes into making one cup of tea is not always known let alone appreciated.
title: Excellent shopping worth the stopover

body: It was a reasonable place who want to know about the history of Ceylon tea. Recommended for tourists.
title: Know the way of ceylon tea

body: Quite a small factory tour of the tea process. A must do while in Sri Lanka but not an impressive overview of the tea world. Good to try the different teas.
title: You have to see the home of tea

body: We liked the place, it isnt perfect , but it can be very good background before visiting the tea factory
title: Very intristing- not impresive

body: The title says it all, and it left much to the imagination. We were the only pair in the museum when we visited and this made our visit very quiet and seem strange. The entrance fee also includes a pot of tea at the end of the tour. Alternative drinks were offered, but those had to be paid for. Our guide told us about the various machines, but it was much more interesting (and free) when we went to a working tea factory.
title: Tea museum

body: The museum is filled with old tea making machines. It is interesting for the first room or two, but then it becomes a bit tedious. Our guide droned on about these machines in a monotone like she had given this presentation a thousand times before. The best thing of all was the tea tasting at the end of the tour. Overall, meh.
title: Somewhat Interesting

body: We enjoyed our visit to the tea museum. It was made that much more informative with the help of our guide. Worth the time to visit.
title: This is how they make tea

body: We stopped here on our way to the botanical gardens.I don't drink tea and my husband didn't before we went to Sri Lanka. However it was very interesting to learn about tea production.We bought a few teas which we took home and my husband subsequently enjoyed.Our guide was pleasant, I felt a bit for her like she had said the same thing over and over again.It's an interesting way to spend an hour and learn about the islands tea industry.
title: Tea Museum

body: Really interesting place, beautiful scenery and interesting tour with friendly, knowledgable staff. Free tea at the end too :) And lovely gift shop area with no pressure to buy, although we got a few bits.
title: Absolutely LOVED this!

body: We got to do our own tea picking and stay in this lovely Converted factory. It's at the very top of a lovely quaint village.
title: Tea plantation

body: This was a guided tour by a very informative pleasant friendly guide.wellworthwhile if you are interested in bygone days.Once the tour has finished you are able to continue and look without the guide.A free cup of tea is available after the completion of the tour.Lovely views from the top floor.Cannot remember exactly how much the entrance fee was but it was not exorbitant.We took a tuk tuk to the museum which cost 600 rupees
title: An insight into tea production in years gone by

body: We arrived just in time to join a small guided tour of the old tea factory, which has 5 floors and is well maintained. The short tour gave us a good overview of how tea is made, and all the machinery was really interesting and in good condition. After the brief tour, we had a free cup of tea and were then left to browse through the whole building again at our leisure. Well worth the 400 rupees (£2) entry fee.
title: Worth a visit.

body: There is a guided tour and the guide explains all the machines etc but once finished you can wander around at leisure. Tour finished with a free cup of tea though you had to pay for the iced tea.....it was very informative if a bit lacking in atmosphere.
title: Fascinating insight into the history of tea in Sri Lanka and how it went from field to packet!

body: Our informative and pleasant guide explained the process of producing tea leaves very well. The old machinery is very interesting. The included cup of tea at the end of the tour was very much appreciated. Well worth a visit.
title: Very interesting

body: An interesting introduction to any tea tours on the way to Hill Country, in an old tea factory. However, the same information more or less you can get for free in the working factories, so you can avoid the steep ticket or the detour.
title: Interesting tea introduction

body: I had two plans arriving in Kandy, since I have been here many times; visit the Ceylon Tea Museum & for the 2nd time travel to Peradeniya Botanical Gardens since I haven't been there since 2010. I KNOW it's +/- 4 kms from Kandy & I thought I could take a bus BUT my hotel manager said there are NO buses to Ceylon Tea Museum. (WRONG!) anyway, he arranged a tuk-tuk for RS 600/RS 800. I got two different prices. Since I have NO clue how long it will take to “see” it the tuk-tuk driver was SUPPOSED to wait & drive me back to Kandy. Once there he follows me (I can tell “time IS money) & he wants to get back. I'm in the middle of the tour and haven't even had a pot of tea. I give him RS 500, since he was SUPPOSED to wait but he wants MORE! “Give me RS 800”, he says. I give him RS 800 & tell him to “take off”, I'll walk back. Creep!!!! I finish the tour, look around the old paintings/posters and have a pot of tea. Then I walk outside to cane to Kandy. I see a bus going up the hill & hope one will go back down to Kandy later on. Lucky me, bus # 655 comes by 30” later and for a whole RS 16 I get a ride to the bus station. FYI; IF you go to a tea plantation it's better than here as there is NO actual tea. There are tea plants outside but it is just a museum. It's only $5+ dollars, man. It is better you go where they are in reality processing tea.
title: Maybe worth a trip but better go to one that is not a museum.

body: Really a nice place to visit with the lovely fragrance of tea and many more.. Very friendly staff ...
title: lovely.. spontanious

body: We couldnt see the functioning factor as it was Holiday time and people were out of the city with their family. But we did visit the factory and saw the machinery. Its a must to visit place and very nicely preserved. Also different types of tea that is been made there. Its worth going. And if you are a Tea Lover to buy some Ceylon Tea you would love it..
title: "Good Attraction "

body: Great informative chance to see how tea is made and all the old machines from the British colonial times. Would be 5* but where is the food in the "restaurant" should be rebranded as a tea room as that all that was served... Not even a biscuit in sight!
title: Insightful

body: This is nice museum and has some really interesting exhibits. What spoilt it for me was that lady guide, that just whisked us around, without really giving any information, other than a rehersed speech. Maybe it was the English barrier, but I felt that she was only interested in getting the tour over. You can go around after and have another look properly, and I would definately encourage you to do just that. There are alot of interesting exhibhits that really do require you to read the plaques.Questions that I asked were not answered fully and did not invite further discussion.There is a tea room at the top, where you can sample some tea (although you can't choose which one). They offer no edibles with the tea, and I feel if they offered light bites, they would certainly do well. I suggested this to them.The plaques are all in English, and this seemed rather strange. I would have thought it would have been in both languages. Worth a visit, but don't expect too much from your guide
title: A good museum but poor guiding inside

body: Housed in a formed tea processing factory, the museum has very well preserved machinery, good labeling, a nice working miniature model, and a pleasant tasting cafe. We got a very nice tour from one of the museum's docents (whom we tipped but were not charged additional beyond high admission fee). It's a classy and pleasant place to spend some time. However, without any machines running or workers running around, you will not get a sense of what a working factory feels like. (I've been to one elsewhere.) It's also up a long and winding road from Kandy so while the views are nice, the drive takes some time and is a bit jarring.
title: Nicely preserved; helpful docent; no sense of factory

body: If you visit a working tea factory add this to the itinerary as it gives an idea of the early days. That said a lot of the machinery was still in use in the actual tea factory we visited, mostly British dating from 1950.A well presented museum and the tour ends with a cup of tea!Guide was clearly knowledgeable but at times her diction was difficult to understand.She had another tour waiting so preliminary guided tour was rather too pacy, but wandering around on your own is easy because everything has a written explanation. Pictures of tea pioneers and how they got machinery in and tea out were priceless.
title: Might be a museum but not much has changed!

body: i visited this place with my some cliants from nederland.germen and french.after visiting this place they was really happy. because of that i believe.they found everything what they was expected.
title: good

body: This is a great little museum, dealing mostly with the processing of tea once it's been picked, and the history of tea cultivation in Sri Lanka. It's very clean and very well laid out. A guide showed us around first, and then left us to explore things in more detail. One disappointment was that there weren't any tea plants around, so it's not terribly scenic; it really is just the factory. (Location: A few kilometers out of Kandy, up in the hills. We paid 500 LKR in taxi fair one-way from the center of Kandy.)
title: Pleasant few hours looking at and old factory and learning about tea

body: A place you should visit to get a glimpse of the main reason Srilanka is famous around the world, the history of Ceylon Tea.. to make it more exsiting and complete, you get a chance to taste the real thing..
title: A lovely place with great historical value

body: What a great little museum. The ticket price includes a quick guided tour by one of the guides. They explain the tea making process and the different machines and then point out a few interesting things on each floor then leave you alone to browse and read in detail anything that takes your interest. The view from the top floor where you drink a lovely cup of Ceylon tea is also worth your time!
title: Interesting!

body: Having been to Nuwara Eliya and spent the whole day passing through and stopping on different tea plantations to drink a cup of tea and go around and listen to a lady dressed in their national costume and explain to you how tea is being processed, you would want to give this place a visit. The Ceylon Tea Museum in Hantana is a bit of a climb (well, I haven't literally climbed it as I was riding in a car, but the road's a bit steep and its recommended to get a tuktuk because its a bit far from the main road of Kandy), but worth the visit if you're truly interested in the history of Ceylon Tea. There were only a few visitors when I visited the place. Not very crowded compared to the tea plantations I've visited in Nuwara Eliya. Here, you'll find the very first tea packet, the first machinery used to produce tea in the land, the story on how Sir James Taylor started the tea industry in Sri Lanka and even one of the first tea shrubs ever. The experience was overwhelming as you could see how the tea industry in the country has evolved from manually grinding and drying the tea leaves to the modern way used in tea plantations nowadays. It's definitely a must-go place for tea lovers like me. There's a pot of tea that awaits you at the end of the tour.
title: History of Tea

body: IF you're interested in a bit of the history of the British in Sri Lanka, how the tea business was set up and operated, in having a nice tuk tuk ride out of town and in buying some tea from source, this nice old wooden factory on a hillside ticks all the boxes. Clean and nicely presented museum with plenty of original tea processing machinery and storage facilities etc, plus a decent selection of historical imagery, documents, posters, tea pots, you name it....to stare it, and a decent cuppa too. There is an entry charge.
title: Tea story

body: We went to this museum on the advice of the tour book. It was worth it in that we gained a great understanding of the history of tea, the processing of tea, and were able to sample this magical brew. It was very interesting and surprising. Well worth the trip. It seems as though the Sri Lankan government doesn't really care if people go to this site or not as there is little to no signage and the road getting there is ridiculous.
title: Ceylon Tea Museum

body: Save yourself the tuk tuk fare by doing the travel this way. It is definitely worth a trip and although it is hard to appreciate the machinery without seeing an active factory, it definitely provides you with an overview of the process and some insightful history about the origins of tea planting in Sri Lanka.It's also a good spot to buy some tea, but be prepared to hustle!
title: Worth the trip! Make this part of your trip onto other destinations (e.g airport)

body: Make sure you try and visit this museum, housed in an old tea factory. The exhibits are in a good state and you do come away much better informed about everything to do with tea. You even get a free cup of delicious tea afterwards and there are a few nice little shops on the upper floor.
title: Really interesting and informative

body: Compared to other tea factories in the central highlands, this one was very average. At 800rp per person it was several times more pricey than other places, and it's more of a historical place than anything else. It is just an old building with traditional machines inside. The tour is ok but quite brief and the tea they give you afterwards isn't very nice... you don't get to choose what tea you get, and if you ask for milk they give you milk powder. The tea factories we visited in Ella and Nuwara Eliya are so much more informative and interesting, and way cheaper.
title: A bit boring and very overpriced

body: Well worth the tuk tuk ride out of Kandy. A beautiful spot and real insight into the history of tea and how it is made.
title: A great museum

body: It was a nice visit. Nothing too spectacular but still worthwhile. Website and travel book info is slightly outdated:Admission: Rs 800Opening hrs: Tue-Sat 8:30 to 15:30hGood 10min Tuk Tuk drive from center
title: Nice visit - see key info below

body: A very interesting and worthwhile excursion. The tea museum contained so much history and the guides were very knowledgeable and friendly. The guides also spoke very good English.You get a free tea at the museum however it took 30 mins for us to receive a cup of tea! Very annoying when the waitress was not doing anything (except standing around) while we waited.
title: Lovely guides, inefficient tea service

body: Took about an hour and was worth the trip. We felt the tour could have included more info on the history, this was a little sparse. The setting is lovely and is great to see how tea is produced. The staff are friendly and laid back. Is a short ride up from kandy town. You can catch a tuk tuk, but note that a bus is just as easy going up and back and will save you a bit of money
title: Worth the effort

body: Set high in the hills of a working tea plantation, this massive former tea factory preserves historic processing equipment and is full of exhibits and stories about tea. A visit begins with a tour, then you can wander around on your own. Ticket cost of Rs. 800 also includes a pot of good tea. The 3-kilometer drive up Hantane Road is very scenic as it twists through hills up to the tea plantation and museum. I did it on a bicycle, slowly and with low gears!
title: Great place to learn about tea!

body: We visited the Ceylon Tea Museum in the afternoon, following the hectic hustle and bustle of Kandy-life and it proved a fantastic getaway for an hour or two. The museum is a converted tea factory, which is gorgeous in itself, and the display of machinery is just amazing. The guided tour was great - the guide such a lovely lady and with excellent English to answer all our questions. The history of tea in Sri Lanka was presented very well with all sorts of tea-related paraphernalia throughout the ages on display. The building and exhibits are maintained extremely well (nice to see the displays and building being taken care of compared to some other museums in the country). The tea shops and tasting on the top two floors are worth visiting. We spent over an hour here. It was very quiet when we went at 1pm, only a handful of visitors, but beware, the museum closes earlier than other Kandian site (3pm that day I think). Great views of Kandy from the road up there too!
title: Excellent visit to Ceylon Tea Museum

body: Great museum- with a full working model of the factory- They have a very friendly staff to give you a full tour of the machinery and you get a free cup of tea at the end. Really enjoyed seeing the factory.
title: Tea Trip

body: 800rp to get it but it's well worth it. We had a great tour which is included in the cost. The woman's English was very good and she explained how the tea was produced, something which wouldn't have been apparent without her explanation. The second top floor is the gift shop. They take you to the floor briefly to say you are welcome to buy something afterwards but don't pressure you at all. On the top floor you get a complimentary pot of tea. You can then go back down and look at all the stuff that was missed during the tour. I highly recommend. Lots of antique tea equipment and the building itself is beautiful.
title: Old timey tea factory

body: This museum gives me history of tea in sri lanka, how to process tea leaf into our mug, and ended with a cup of tea. Clean place but the toilet. Has some tea souvenir shop in it. With Lkr 800 entrance fee, they also guide us into the museum and also for a cup of tea. I also spent 800Lkr for tuktuk from kandy station to this museum and the tuktuk driver wait for me while I'm in it and return to kandy station.
title: Interesting place for learning tea

body: Really enjoyed it here, good info providedNice to see all this old machines and methods, and after the tour a nice cup of tea.Pathway to Tea museum needs to be renewed.
title: Very interesting.

body: This was a brief but interesting tour followed by the big sell in the tea shop. The tea is hugely, hugely overpriced but the little tour was informative.
title: Enjoyable. Expectations that you will purchase!

body: The Ceylon Tea Museum offers a lot of information about the history of teaproduction in Sri Lanka and about manufactoring. The building is on top of a hill not far from the citycenter of Kandy. It offers a stunning view above at this place. The building is an old factory and you can see the original machines there. You will get a guided tour in the four story wooden building. At the top level is a café where a cup of tea is offered for free. You can also watch a documentary about tea there. At the third level are some shops with a big variety of tea for reasonable prices. The entrance fee is 750 rupies and worth it. Your driver will get free entry and also a cup of tea. You should plan about two hours for the visit.
title: very charming place with lots of information

body: We visited a tea plantation south of Kandy, but were pleased that we'd visited here (Ceylon Tea Museum) first. It was informative and our guide (provided by the venue) was helpful. Nice free cuppa at the end of the trip, too.
title: Enjoyable and informative visit

body: There are several tea factories in and around Kandy, however the tea museum is more than a factory. It follows the introduction of tea to Sri Lanka, the history of its production, giants in the tea industry who have influenced the name of Ceylon tea. After the tour, you get to have a nice cuppa too.
title: Seen the plantations? Now see what happens to it

body: This museum gives you a really good history and background to how tea came to Sri Lanka. As well as housing the machines that they used to use to process the tea. Interesting visit. We were the only ones there when we went which made for more of a private tour.
title: Full History of Tea Making

body: The Ceylon Tea Museum is one of it kind and is a must visit in kandy, it gives the history of tea and also about the different type of tea in the region
title: A Eye opener to the history of tea

body: nice beautifully restored machines, clean and personal tour guide provided, tea and tea paraphernalia for sale.
title: nicely detailed tour of tea manufacturing

body: We spent an hour or so visiting the Museum and found it really interesting, BUT .... our Guide (who was very sweet) whisked us through the tea process and surprise surprise ended up in the shop!! We actually then went back through the museum and found some lovely facts, artefacts and memorabilia. What was lacking was a tea bush, real tea leaves, how they grow etc ... it's all based on what happens when they arrive at the processing plant. This could be so much better - instead we felt that the aim was to get you in to buy (second rate?) tea.
title: Worth a visit but lacking tea!!!

body: Myself and a friend visited on a Sunday morning-it was quiet with only a handful of other visitors. It closes on Sundays at 3pm. The guide was warm and friendly but we felt that the site could do a lot more to improve the experience by showing machinery actually working with tea leaves being sifted, dried and roasted etc in front of us. An interactive experience, if you will. At the end of the 15 minute tour over 3 floors(not suitable for people with a physical disability as a lot of stairs to climb) we went for our free cup of tea on the top floor. This was a huge disappointment. The cups and saucers had obviously just been hand washed from the previous visitor as they were still wet and not dried. The tea itself was not boiled. Note ;water for tea is meant to be boiled!
title: Good visit but room for inprovement

body: Your visit to SriLanka cannot be complete without a visit to a tea plantation or tea factory.However, I dont urge you to buy anything from these places because products are extremely overpriced!! Be sure that the guide and tour organizing company who take you there get a percentage of whatever you buy!!!!
title: Interesting to visit

body: Buffet dinner was very expensive it was for 75 US Dollars per person. Breakfast was very good and have several items.
title: We stayed there for one night.

body: The tour takes place in an original old building with old machinery etc present. It is a little 'dry' as an experience but still didn't regret going as the guide was excellent and enhanced the experience. Very quiet at the tine of our visit - only 2 couples including us! Had tea afterwards as part of the tour - probably the best tea I had the whole holiday. All staff extremely warm and friendly. There are reasonably priced teas to buy if desired but absolutely no pressure.
title: visited as part of tour of the island

body: The museum gives a nice insight in tea manufacturing. The guide was very friendly and knew a lot. We liked the visit but would not go to Kandy for this place only.
title: Nice to visit when in the neighborhood

body: You get a shirt free guided tour through the factory. Afterwards, you can enjoy a complimentary tea and buy souvenirs.
title: Worth a visit

body: We were looking forward to coming here to see the tea being picked and how it is sold to everywhere in the world from being picked to the different processes to making tea,we found it very interesting to watch the pickers and the process of the tea harvest.Amazing scenery of the tea plantations and of the river valley from a view point.Take a warm jumper or jacket as it does get quite cold as very high up.And if you are lucky your visit will coincide with a slice of cake and a free tea tasting.Well worth going.
title: Interesting visit

body: I finally got the whole proces of tea making. Did trips to museums before but was never completely satisfied. At this one the proces is very clearly explained and there is plenty of room for questions which were answered to satisfaction. They were not pushy on us visiting the shops and we got a nice pot of tea after the tour. The building is beautiful! Worth the trip!
title: I finally got it!

body: Without any doubts this museum is the best in town. You can understand a lot about the most British drink, tea. A guide will bring you through the old factory. The building is very old and interesting. It's possible to visit some plantation outside
title: The best museum in Kandy

body: The museum now charges 750p (not 500) for entry. You get 15mins tour and a complimentary cup of tea. All the machines are not operational. A few more exhibits related to tea making (e.g. some of the belongings of the founders of the tea business on the island) and some info panels. The toilets there are disgusting. I'd recommend visiting Pedro Tea Factory in Nuwara Elya instead (which is for 200rp and much nicer, also not operating during visiting hours, but there is at least some actual tea there) or other tea factories where you can actually see the process of making tea.
title: Overpriced

body: Excellent tour guide explanation of the old, mostly English machinery used in the tea process. Husband loved it as he knew many of the manufactuners. Perhaps just as good to see the machines here, still mostly the same used in working factories now, rather than go to a working one.Enjoyable and not thronged with people like the "major factories". Lots of historical info and lovely old photos displayed, oh yes - and you get a cup of tea too!
title: Interesting historically

body: if you are in kandy, this is worth visiting. its not a tea factory so dont expect to see real time tea production. this is all about tea and its history in sri lanka. they do sell tea there and we never found it being sold any where else. good to try
title: interesting and educational trip

body: An amazing trip to the beginnings and later history of tea growing amd making in Sri Lanka. The facilitie are a little sparse and the road access road from the main road is in extremely poor condition. However, with a guided toor and free cuppa at the end, it is a very interesting and worthwhile trip.
title: Well worth the effort

body: Set up in the hills outside Kandy, this tea museum is well worth a visit. Not big on tea tasting, this gives more of a historical view and a greater understanding of the processes involved in tea making and production.
title: Interesting historical tea museum

body: Well maintained old factory site with original equipment in place to provide an interesting insight into the development of the tea industry in Sri Lanka. Provides some understandings about the tea we buy, and provides a tasting, and the opportunity to buy some souvenir teas on site. The guide had a good understanding of the site, and the tour was well organised. There is a small charge for the tour.
title: Interesting glimpse of the tea industry

body: The Ceylon Tea Museum is a very authentic museum to understand how tea is made and distinguish between the different kinds of tea. The tour was ok. The shops are a good place to buy some tea as a souvenir as they offer a great selection for descent prices.
title: Very nice visit

body: This is a former tea factory, now converted into a museum, about 15 mins. from Kandy. Great insights into the history of tea in Ceylon (shout out to Mr. Lipton of Lipton Tea fame; a few photos of him in one portion). Guide is knowledgeable about the history and processing of tea. Miniature model of entire factory is also cool. Guide goes from room to room and ends the tour (30-45 mins.) inviting you to a cup of tea in the cafe, after which you are welcome to linger about to read/take pix at your own pace. LKR 500 entry fee and well worth it. Only sour note: manager said that we could pay here to go see a tea factory a few kms. farther up the road; didn't make sense, so we didn't pay, and good that we didn't as the other factory turned out to be defunct; not sure what he was playing at.
title: Educational and Informative

body: I liked this place because you can get some knowledge about machines and techniques which were used for producing tea. The guide was very nice, but she was rather in a hurry. We enjoyed the cups of tea we got at the top of the museum and bought some packets of tea in the shops. There were several different shopes in the middle floor so you can compare the prices and kinds of tea before you choose some which is good.
title: Good

body: We are not the only ones to discover that the location of this museum is wrong in the Lonely Planet guide 13th ed, page 159. There Ceylon Tea Museum is marked with #1 close to Sarasav Uvana railway station. That is wrong, see google maps It is close to Hantana D2-D3 on the map. If you are wrong a and have ended up in Peradeniya a tuktuk driver will bring you to the real spot for 1000 lkr. Another issue is that this museum is close to Ceylon Tea Estates which have received a better rating in Tripadvisor , has a different address yet Google maps places them close together. The tour through the museum is Okish, but rather I would have seen the real works instead of old machines.
title: Map location in Lonely Planet is wrong

body: Very detailed overview of tea making process. Each step is clearly explained and the staff is eager to share their knowledge and show the machines and how they work.
title: Great tea house with good explanation!

body: We arrived after a hairy ride up on a tuk tuk and were immediately given a very knowledgeable tour guide with amazing English skills. She showed us around and explained the tea making process. Whilst it was a little rushed, she answered our questions and we had time at the end to go back and revisit the things we didn't have time to peruse the first time around. On the top floor there's a room where they serve you a cup of tea (included in the price) and you can look out over the mountains. It really is incredible and, even if you're not that interested in tea, it makes a nice jaunt outside of the centre of Kandy. There is a floor dedicated to the selling of tea - you can wander around or miss it entirely. There's no hard sell.
title: Interesting with Great Views

body: Elegantly clad in saris, the ladies at the museum run the show....Entrance fee keeps increasing, but there is only that much to the factory and the tea. Lots of info about machinery as well as documents and valuable items belonging to the long gone past. The many stairs to walk up during tour are worth climbing, as on the top floor you are rewarded with a free cup of fresh Ceylon tea and an audio-visual presentation about - tea. And then there are tea boutiques set up on the floor just below top floor. Mesmerizing! But one thing to remember: the museum closes at 4 pm!
title: informative

body: They will charge you a ticket which is expensive. you can enjoy the same experience actually even better with real tea leaves at Glenloch for free on your way back from elephant bath towards Colombo. the tea shops are interesting in the museum but Glenloch also have good collection of tea with free tasting of different tea.
title: was not really impressed

body: For kids it good ...as it educates and gives a complete tour on how tea is produced . in the end theres a shop from where you can buy.overall nothing to stop by during the visit in sri lanka
title: tea garden

body: One of the well organized informative mesuem about origin story of Sri Lanka tea (Ceylon tea). The staff was friendly and we'll educated to provide a great history lesson from James Taylor to tea brewing.
title: Back in time with tea.

body: From august 1st onward The Ceylon Tea Museum will be opened every days of the week.It's good to come before the closing hour as there are many visitors around.
title: Opening days for the Kandy Perahera festive season

body: What a peaceful, welcome respite from being treated like a walking ATM in Sri Lanka! The staff here are so lovely and welcoming and it's set in a beautiful location about a 20 minute tuk tuk ride from Kandy's centre. The tour was very informative and interesting and the guide equally so. The museum holds some impressive tea history, including the first tea drier in Sri Lanka. The complimentary pot of tea is lovely (we could have done with some milk though). The view from the top of the museum is also stunning and there's some nice tea shops located at the top also, if you're a tea enthusiast.
title: If you like tea and history, this place is ace!

body: This seems to contradict other reviews but to be honest its not that great. Yes, you can get a cheap bus up there and the trip up there alone is of course worth the SLR15 each but the climax is just a bit disappointing. The museum tour is literally 10 minutes and focuses only on the machines stored within museum, at the expense of the history behind the industry which when is addressed seems to ignore colonialism...bit odd. Go if you have an extra day in Kandy otherwise I would just stay in town, get some short eats and drink a cup of Ceylon tea in the real world.
title: Would be average but for the price its poor

body: My husband planned it because he wished both kids to see how actually tea was originated. We loved the guide and we loved the British era building very well kept too. The tea they offer actually opens your eyes that what crap actually multinational companies are serving you in the name of finest tea.We bought loads of tea from there.Must visit if you believe in the quality of life.
title: Must visit with little kids.

body: If you drink tea and would like to see the process of drying and machinery involved, this one is a must visit. They have a decent variety of tea leaves and they are happy to answer your questions. The tour begins from the ground floor and when you reach the top floor, you are served a complimentary cup of tea. They also have a small shop for people to buy tea samples and accessories. I did buy some flavoured and Ceylon tea packets from the place and they were good. However I did find later that you could buy it cheaper elsewhere! Not sure why the price difference when the factory should be the cheapest; but overall it was worth the visit. A must do in Kandy.
title: A must visit for the complimentary cuppa if nothing else!

body: Avoid the other tea shops that all the tour buses go to. This working factory gives you a tour guide, teaches you about tea and gives you a nice cup of tea at the end of the short and simple tour. The shop has many teas to buy and take home and there is no need for asking for a discount. Great experience for tea lovers and non -tea lovers alike.
title: Best place for tea in Kandy

body: there are different tea factories and make sure the tuk tuk takes you to the correct location , tell them it is the government tea museum
title: Kandy is a town based of plantation industry

body: This is a Ceylon tea factory. Take a round to see that the tea is made from the leaves. They make different quality of tea and the same is offered to buy.
title: a tea factory

body: From clocktower you can take a local bus to the museum. Its 750 R entrance, good guide and a big pot of tea is included.Interessting place and a good place to buy different kinds of local tea ( not expensive at all).
title: Nice to visit

body: it was actually a tea factory which was turned in to a museum. its the factory which has James Taylor's (first person to plant tea in Sri Lanka) equipments and things he used. you can see the machines there. it will cost you 750 LKR ($15) if you are not a local. its well worth it. the ladies who are there will explain how you make tea and you really can learn a lot from them. you can even to tea tasting and buy tea and enjoy a cup as well. many tour operators or guides will not take you to this place cause they will not get a commission out of your purchases. just 5km away from Temple tooth and easy to find.
title: want to know about TEA then this is the place

body: I really enjoyed my visit here. Find out all about tea and how Sri Lanka was nearly known for its coffee rather than its tea. The show you all the machines used for making tea then you go on to have a large pot of tea (included) and a look around a museum with informative displays. Plenty of tea to purchase on site too.
title: Drink tea and learn about tea

body: We walked up from our guesthouse to this museum and it was a pleasant guided tour. Unfortunately the museum closes at 4:30pm and we therefore did not have enough time to see all of it.
title: Fun museum

body: a fabulous afternoon seeing from the tree the leaves being picked and how it is processed to the end and then a lovely cup of tea, in my top 3 for places to visit
title: fabulous

body: This is a place to visit if you love tea and if you wanna know how they used to prepare tea from the colonial times. Not far from Kandy and the road is good! It offers great collection of old machinery and methods used to make tee from tea leaves. On the top floor it have a great view with a tea shop. The telescope up in the top floor is adding some value to the setup. One could observe Kandy city through it.
title: Great view, Lots of History and cool top floor tea shop!

body: To understand the tea in your teacup you must come here Lthough they no longer process tea. The young lady was informative and showed and explained all the machinery involved in the process from bush to your cup. The museum is a bit quaint but if you embrace the tour it is interesting. On 4 levels, there is no lift, so only the ground floor is suitable for the physically challenged! 5$ p.p. this includes a pot/cup of tea at the end on the 4th where there is a very interesting film of the whole process - history to benefits of tea drinking today. 3rd floor a no "pressure to buy" area. The staff are charming, happy for you to look, not feel obligated to buy. Well done.
title: Quaint

body: There are many tea states in Ceylon . Ceylon was the name of Sri Lanka .here they have a collection of all the different type and Flavours of tea .
title: Ceylon tea museum

body: this is a must visit place. it is a really nice museum with lots to see. pros : the museum building is nice. the equipment used during the era are interesting. there was a tour guide who brought us around. there were a few shops selling tea. there was a cafe which offered free tea. the different types of teas are very interesting. the history of tea is interesting. cons : the tour guide was not as interactive as we would have liked. she just recited what she had to. infact, she did not allow us time to look at the stuff and ask questions. she was more interested in keeping to the time. the free tea offered at the cafe was just given to us in a pot and 2 cups. there was no one to explain what kind of tea it was. there was a video playing but to us, first timers there, it was kinda boring. the shops close at 330pm as the official closing time of the museum is 345pm. you need to have sufficient to look at the articles, and spend some time in the shops. on the whole, it was rather informative. there is a entrance fee.
title: interesting and informative

body: Tea museum helps to travelers to learn more about tea cultivation in srilanka. Specially the history, Tea manufacturing, & Importance of drinking tea.
title: Excellent place to visit

body: This was very interesting to see from start to finish where our cup of tea comes from, we had a guided tour of the factory and then a nice cuppa before we did the gift shop and went on our travels
title: Another part of our tour of Sri Lanka

body: The tea museum showcases the history of tea production in Sri Lanka and variety of tea available. Along with the entrance ticket (which is over-priced), you get to taste a complimentary tea in museum.
title: Insight to tea processing

body: well organised and presented in a lovely building, with superb views from its windows. Enjoyed reading about the history of the tea plantations of Sri Lanka.
title: Tea museum, Kandy

body: The museum will be closed on 13th,14th,15th & 16th April 2016 for the Sinhalese & Hindu new year festival.on 12th it will be closed at 3 p.m.
title: Closing dates for the New year Festival

body: This is a small tea plantation with all the original machinery still in use. We saw where the tea is picked, dried and cut, also where it is packed in sacks for export. We were able to buy some tea to bring home.
title: Original machinery still in use.

body: I think this is a must see even for locals to get an understanding about the inception of the tea industry. The location is in Hantane in Kandy.Ticket is about Rs 100 for a local and Rs 750 for a tourist. There are about 4 levels to this building and the 3rd level has several tea boutiques to purchase tea from... I suggest any tourist to buy tea from this place as its cheaper compared to prices of tea in tourist stores in Colombo.
title: Details about Tea and its industry in a nutshell

body: Worth a trip for a few hours, interesting history of tea in Ceylon. A guide shows you around & gives a general overview of systems involved in processing tea in the early days and the early founders of the area. Free cuppa at the end. Beautiful old building
title: Interesting tour

body: If you are really interested in the tea business or an aficionado of beautifully restored vintage British agricultural machinery, this museum is well worth the effort. We found it to be a worthwhile complement to a visit to a working tea estate up in the mountains. It is very much a static museum, with no processing going on, but our lady guide was charming and informative. Unfortunately, a power cut meant that we didn't get our cup of tea after the visit, but we were glad we went.
title: A must for vintage machinery enthusiasts

body: A short drive out of Kandy the museum is well worth a visit. When we were there a guide accompanied us around the exhibitions telling us about the history of the tea industry in Sri Lanka and provided information on the manufacturing processIncluded in the admission price is a cup of tea
title: History Lesson on Tea Making

body: It is must visit place when you are in kandy Sri Lanka is better known in the world for its finest tea and this the most appropriate place learn about its rich history and to take first hand experience the process in which hard labored tea leaves becoming a nice stimulating beverage in front of your own eyes
title: Must Visit Place

body: Closed Sunday and informed by staff Monday as well. Disappointing and the road heading up to the factory is rough which is atypical of many Kandy roads but far worse. You'd think the government would invest upgrading the roads given tourism is a key driver of the economy but the politicians seem more interested in filling their bank accounts rather developing the economy.
title: Closed Sunday & Monday

body: First, I should identify myself as a museum professional. As such, I couldn't help but see the Ceylon Tea Museum as a facility that could so easily be made excellent. As it is, it's pretty good and a pleasant and enlightening trip from Kandy. Their tour guides are wonderful and enthusiastic, but the tour is strangely out of order. The tea bushes come after seeing the machinery. The miniature factory would have worked better at the beginning or end where it could be used to sum up the tea process. The tea service on the top floor was pleasant, but if you are there with a school group, as we were, you could be waiting forty minutes for a cup - with only an old and overly laudatory video for company. It must be hard to gain buy-in from the museum backers, but I feel like a more critical look into the history of the plantation tamils or even a more in-depth discussion of the work they do would have improved the experience.
title: Interesting, with lots of potential

body: This museum is well done and is in an old tea factory. Downstairs we could see machines and a nice lady explained us how to produce black tea. Upstairs you can read a lot about the history, it is very interesting. Take time to visit and enjoy.
title: A lot to read and discover

body: The guide took her job with more speed than depth but when we started asking questions she answered thoroughly and probably realized we were interested. There are lots of machines and stuff to see. The shops were very different with a couple of them selling mostly gift packs. We found a very good one and the prices were really low. We have more than 2 kgs in our luggade. The tea served at the end of the visit was really good and there was a film about tea. Enjoyed it!
title: Nice visit

body: Presented in an ex tea factory this tells the story of tea production after picking the leaf. Old machinery can be seen and a range of artefacts from the early period of tea production under British control. Quite interesting but not exciting. There is a range of small units selling tea on the upper floor and a small tea bar on the top floor.
title: Nothing to get excited about

body: Good experience to see how the tea is processed. Good explanations and a not too long visit. Can arrive there by tuk-tuk.
title: Good visit

body: Everything you need to know for the tea in Sri Lanka. You can discover the production of tea with all the machines, archives, old photos and few different shops where you can buy locally produced tea. The guide tour is included in the entrance fee of 700 rupees and it's very useful for the tea production area.
title: Museum worth a visit

body: Ceylon the old charming name of the now called "Sri Lanka" is maintained by the good old "Ceylon Tea Museum".The charming Kandy adds dynamism to the Museum, once a tea factory and later redone as a Tea Museum could be one of a kind in the world and allows Tea lovers to experience and walk through their Tea feel..don't miss if you are around in Kandy or Nuwereliyya....
title: The land of good Tea..

body: This place is crazily overpriced. Do not buy anything from here. They lure the customers. It is not worth it.
title: Overpriced

body: You'll never drink a cup of tea the same way again! It's incredible how many stages it goes through. Happy tour guides, lovely views (of course... it's Sri Lanka after all) and a nice cup of the local brew of your choice. I didn't like the sign by management asking not to tip the staff... Don't tell me what to do and also... why? Anyway, it was altogether lovely and I tipped anyway.
